# nbzinbKnight

**nbzinbKnight** fits two models for overdispersed count data,
implementing the estimation from scratch rather than with a
general-purpose optimizer:

- **Negative binomial (NB2) regression**,
  [`nbreg()`](https://knightrt-lgtm.github.io/nbzinbKnight/reference/nbreg.md):
  iteratively reweighted least squares (IRLS) for the coefficients,
  alternated with Newton–Raphson for log(θ). Same model as
  [`MASS::glm.nb()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/MASS/man/glm.nb.html).
- **Zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) regression**,
  [`zinbreg()`](https://knightrt-lgtm.github.io/nbzinbKnight/reference/zinbreg.md):
  an EM algorithm whose M-steps are IRLS fits (a logistic regression for
  the zero-inflation part and a weighted NB fit for the count part).
  Same model as `pscl::zeroinfl(..., dist = "negbin")`.

Both functions reproduce the reference implementations on the
`bioChemists` and `NMES1988` data (see the comparison tests in
`tests/testthat/`). This package was written for the STA 651 final
project.

**Website:** <https://knightrt-lgtm.github.io/nbzinbKnight/>, with the
function reference and the [project
report](https://knightrt-lgtm.github.io/nbzinbKnight/articles/report.html).

## Installation

``` r
# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("knightrt-lgtm/nbzinbKnight")
```

## Usage

``` r
library(nbzinbKnight)
data("bioChemists", package = "pscl")

# Negative binomial regression
fit_nb <- nbreg(art ~ fem + mar + kid5 + phd + ment, data = bioChemists)
summary(fit_nb)

# Zero-inflated negative binomial: count covariates | zero-model covariates
fit_zinb <- zinbreg(art ~ fem + mar + kid5 + phd + ment | ment,
                    data = bioChemists)
summary(fit_zinb)

# Model comparison and prediction
AIC(fit_nb, fit_zinb)
predict(fit_zinb, newdata = bioChemists[1:5, ], type = "zero")  # P(structural zero)
```

Both fits support `print`, `summary`, `coef`, `vcov`, `logLik`,
`AIC`/`BIC`, `fitted`, `residuals` (Pearson and response), `nobs`, and
`predict`. [`predict()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/predict.html) for ZINB
fits supports `type = "response"` ((1 − π)μ), `"count"` (μ), and
`"zero"` (π).

## R CMD check

[`devtools::check()`](https://devtools.r-lib.org/reference/check.html)
finishes with 0 errors, 0 warnings, and 0 notes.

# Package index

## Negative binomial regression

NB2 regression fitted by IRLS for beta and Newton-Raphson for
log(theta).

- [`nbreg()`](https://knightrt-lgtm.github.io/nbzinbKnight/reference/nbreg.md)
  : Negative binomial regression by IRLS and Newton-Raphson

- [`nbreg_control()`](https://knightrt-lgtm.github.io/nbzinbKnight/reference/nbreg_control.md)
  :

  Control parameters for
  [`nbreg()`](https://knightrt-lgtm.github.io/nbzinbKnight/reference/nbreg.md)

- [`print(`*`<nbreg>`*`)`](https://knightrt-lgtm.github.io/nbzinbKnight/reference/nbreg-methods.md)
  [`summary(`*`<nbreg>`*`)`](https://knightrt-lgtm.github.io/nbzinbKnight/reference/nbreg-methods.md)
  [`print(`*`<summary.nbreg>`*`)`](https://knightrt-lgtm.github.io/nbzinbKnight/reference/nbreg-methods.md)
  [`coef(`*`<nbreg>`*`)`](https://knightrt-lgtm.github.io/nbzinbKnight/reference/nbreg-methods.md)
  [`vcov(`*`<nbreg>`*`)`](https://knightrt-lgtm.github.io/nbzinbKnight/reference/nbreg-methods.md)

## Zero-inflated negative binomial regression

ZINB regression fitted by an EM algorithm with IRLS M-steps.

- [`zinbreg()`](https://knightrt-lgtm.github.io/nbzinbKnight/reference/zinbreg.md)
  : Zero-inflated negative binomial regression by EM with IRLS M-steps
